calls.head: Benson’s line gets the soft minutes
calls.body: At home, the Sabres keep sending Benson’s line (Quinn, Östlund and Benson) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Lindy Ruff has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Mammoth’s second line is Lee, Guenther and Cooley.

calls.head: Don’t buy Vejmelka’s record against the Sabres
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Vejmelka has been a wall against the Sabres, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Sabres finally get to him.
calls.call: If Vejmelka starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .896 than to his .929 against the Sabres.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Mammoth take down the Sabres
paras: Kailer Yamamoto played his first game of the season, after missing the first five. Tage Thompson got the scoring started for the Sabres on the power play midway through the first. Yamamoto made it 1-1, 2:12 later. Nick Schmaltz, Anders Lee and John Marino scored three goals in 6:22 late in the second to put the Mammoth up 4-1.
The Mammoth drove the play, outshooting the Sabres 30-24, and the scoreboard caught up. Karel Vejmelka made 23 saves for the Mammoth, and Colten Ellis stopped 26 of 30.
MacKenzie Weegar and Peyton Krebs squared off late in the second. Vejmelka picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Mammoth improved to 4-2-0, and the Sabres dropped to 2-3-0.

items.text: Clayton Keller extended his point streak against Buffalo to six games.
The Mammoth have beaten the Sabres five straight times, going back to 2024-25.
